gen_risks.description: Political instability, active conflict, and unrest in FCV regions (such as Northwest/Southwest Cameroon and CAR) may restrict project access, threaten staff safety, and disrupt healthcare delivery.
gen_risks.mitigation: Develop and implement country-specific Security Management Plans, engage local community leaders, utilize flexible operational procedures, and deploy third-party monitoring in conflict-affected zones.
gen_risks.evidence: Political instability, particularly in the North-West and South-West regions, may disrupt service delivery

gen_risks.description: Financial management control weaknesses and decentralized project implementation in remote areas create risks of ineligible expenses, unvouched transactions, and questionable expenditures.
gen_risks.mitigation: Customize accounting software across PIUs within three months of effectiveness, conduct quarterly risk-based internal audits, hire independent external auditors, and update financial manuals.
gen_risks.evidence: several activities under the project like workshops, trainings and the local-level capacity building are at risk to generate questionable expenditures

gen_risks.description: Weak contract management, administrative inefficiencies, and low market competition in fragile contexts may cause significant procurement delays for key laboratory supplies and equipment.
gen_risks.mitigation: Conduct early market engagement, standardize procurement documentation, build PIU contract management capacity, track progress via STEP in real time, and explore joint regional procurements.
gen_risks.evidence: Procurement Risks include delays, governance issues, weak contract management, and limited market competition in fragile settings.

gen_risks.description: Expanded health facility and laboratory operations could generate hazardous medical, chemical, and biological waste, leading to environmental contamination and public health hazards if mishandled.
gen_risks.mitigation: Update and implement Healthcare Biomedical Waste Management Plans, apply ESMF screening guidelines, upgrade waste disposal facilities, and train laboratory personnel in biosafety and biosecurity.
gen_risks.evidence: laboratories will be supplied with reagents, chemicals, and equipment that may constitute medical waste once used

gen_risks.description: Increased deployment of project workers and community health personnel into local areas heightens the risk of Sexual Exploitation, Abuse, and Sexual Harassment (SEA/SH).
gen_risks.mitigation: Recruit dedicated GBV specialists, implement country-specific SEA/SH Action Plans, enforce worker codes of conduct, and establish survivor-centered grievance redress mechanisms.
gen_risks.evidence: The overall project SEA/SH risks are judged to be substantial

gen_risks.description: Capacity constraints, institutional governance gaps, and understaffing within Ministry of Health Project Implementation Units (PIUs) may delay project execution and reporting.
gen_risks.mitigation: Establish dedicated PIUs with qualified coordinators, procurement, FM, and E&S specialists, and provide targeted technical assistance and cross-country peer-to-peer capacity building.
gen_risks.evidence: Institutional capacity gaps remain a significant concern, necessitating targeted efforts to improve governance and FM in the health sector.

gen_risks.description: Frequent extreme weather events, such as severe flooding and heatwaves, can damage healthcare infrastructure and trigger sudden outbreaks of waterborne and vector-borne diseases.
gen_risks.mitigation: Incorporate green, climate-resilient building standards into infrastructure refurbishments, install solar energy and WASH systems, and link climate data to disease surveillance.
gen_risks.evidence: Climate change contributed to at least 50 percent of natural disasters registered in Cameroon, CAR, Chad, and RoC

gen_risks.description: Complexity in multi-country and inter-institutional coordination between regional bodies (CEMAC, WAHO) and national line ministries could impede regional data sharing and joint surveillance.
gen_risks.mitigation: Formalize cross-border collaboration MoUs, operationalize the Regional Coordination Committee (RCC) facilitated by CEMAC and WAHO, and establish standardized information-sharing protocols.
gen_risks.evidence: Effective coordination among CEMAC, national governments, and beneficiaries is essential for successful implementation.

gen_risks.description: Inadequate stakeholder consultation or failure to include vulnerable and indigenous populations could result in inequitable access to health security interventions and community grievances.
gen_risks.mitigation: Implement country-tailored Stakeholder Engagement Plans (SEPs), establish operational Grievance Redress Mechanisms (GRMs), and deliver inclusive, community-based risk communications.
gen_risks.evidence: inadequate stakeholder engagement to properly inform design and implementation; (ii) the exclusion of vulnerable or disadvantaged groups

gen_risks.description: Large influxes of refugees and internally displaced persons escaping regional conflict can overwhelm local health services and increase cross-border disease transmission risks.
gen_risks.mitigation: Strengthen surveillance at Points of Entry, deploy mobile health teams to refugee-hosting areas, integrate displaced populations into emergency plans, and coordinate with humanitarian agencies.
gen_risks.evidence: Chad currently hosts over 1.5 million IDPs and refugees due to conflict in Lake Chad Basin and instability in Sudan, CAR, and Libya.

gen_risks.description: Delays in fulfilling dated legal covenants, such as recruiting key specialists, setting up internal/external auditors, and customizing accounting software, could disrupt project disbursements.
gen_risks.mitigation: Closely monitor legal covenant compliance schedules during World Bank supervision, utilize Project Preparation Advances where available, and streamline consultant hiring.
gen_risks.evidence: customize the existing accounting software to include the bookkeeping for the Project... recruit an internal auditor

gen_risks.description: Constrained domestic macro-fiscal capacity and high out-of-pocket health expenditures threaten the financial sustainability of health security infrastructure and operations after project closing.
gen_risks.mitigation: Provide technical assistance to integrate health security into national Medium-Term Expenditure Frameworks, establish expenditure tracking, and support domestic resource mobilization.
gen_risks.evidence: A challenging macro-fiscal outlook and high poverty levels make the region particularly vulnerable to shocks

gen_risks.description: Accelerating Antimicrobial Resistance (AMR) rates and frequent zoonotic pathogen spillovers risk exceeding regional treatment capabilities and emergency containment systems.
gen_risks.mitigation: Operationalize One Health National Action Plans, implement antimicrobial stewardship programs in health facilities, expand genomic sequencing, and conduct joint human-animal risk assessments.
gen_risks.evidence: In CAR, the mortality rate associated with AMR is among the highest in the region... Zoonotic outbreaks across Africa have risen

gen_risks.description: Surges in public health emergencies can severely disrupt routine essential primary healthcare, leading to reduced coverage for maternal and child health, immunizations, and chronic conditions.
gen_risks.mitigation: Adopt and fund national essential health service continuity plans, monitor primary care utilization metrics routinely, and train community health workers to maintain primary care during crises.
gen_risks.evidence: Health emergencies, as was the case for the COVID-19 pandemic, disrupt services like maternal and child health, immunization

gen_risks.description: Severe gaps in laboratory diagnostic facilities, biosafety standards, and biospecimen transportation networks could prevent early identification and containment of epidemic threats.
gen_risks.mitigation: Support laboratory accreditation via SLIPTA, establish secure specimen transport systems, equip reference laboratories, and implement Laboratory Information Management Systems (LIMS).
gen_risks.evidence: the region commonly faces significant gaps in laboratory diagnostic capabilities, disease surveillance and information systems

gen_risks.description: Systemic gender disparities and career advancement barriers may limit female health workers' participation in advanced technical epidemiology training programs.
gen_risks.mitigation: Establish explicit gender recruitment targets for FETP/FELTP/ISAVET programs, conduct targeted outreach to female health staff, and offer flexible training delivery formats.
gen_risks.evidence: women remain underrepresented in formal epidemiological training and decision-making

gt_risks.description: Political and governance risk (Moderate), considering fragility, socio-political instability, violence and weak governance of beneficiary countries.
gt_risks.mitigation: Close engagement by the World Bank to coordinate activities with other key partners.

gt_risks.description: Technical design risk (Substantial), considering the complexities of coordinating national-level and regional-level activities to align and build on each other, and the different levels of readiness at country-level.
gt_risks.mitigation: Exploring the possibility of a coordinated implementation arrangement with CEMAC as the lead technical coordination body for regional activities.

gt_risks.description: Weak institutional capacity for implementation and sustainability (Substantial), combined with overstretched or nonexistent PIUs in respective countries.
gt_risks.mitigation: Strengthening the existing PIUs and intensive capacity building and targeted TA for newly established PIUs.

gt_risks.description: Fiduciary risk (Substantial) due to weak governance structures and inadequate FM systems.
gt_risks.mitigation: Close implementation support by the World Bank, including TA as well as additional training and coaching on fiduciary processes.

gt_risks.description: E&S risk (Substantial) given the security risks associated with service delivery in FCV (fragility, conflict, and violence) settings.
gt_risks.mitigation: Close implementation support by the World Bank, including TA as well as additional training and coaching on managing E&S risks.
